slides.title: One sentence. **Event on sale.**
slides.sub: No new website to learn. Just one app added to the AI.
slides.scene: Phoney the blue phone character sits at a cosy desk next to a tired event organiser with a mug, both looking at a laptop; the organiser is mid-sentence, speaking casually, while Phoney the blue phone character rolls up tiny sleeves eagerly like a waiter about to take an order. Evening light, warm, funny.

slides.label: Without the app
slides.caption: The AI can only explain how **you** might do it yourself.
slides.scene: Phoney the blue phone character stands at a whiteboard covered in long abstract arrows and boxes, lecturing earnestly with a pointer, while the event organiser sits slumped in a chair, slowly sliding off it from boredom, holding an empty to-do list.

items.title: You say it once
items.text: "Set up our October networking night, 80 places, £15 a ticket."

items.title: It asks what it doesn't know
It reads the price back
items.text: So you catch the typo, not your guests.

items.title: On sale only when you say yes
items.text: Nothing goes public on a guess.

slides.label: The bit that matters
slides.caption: It **waits for your yes**. Then the tickets go on sale.
slides.scene: Phoney the blue phone character stands beside a big shiny launch lever with one hand hovering over it, looking up politely at the event organiser who is about to give a thumbs up; a little queue of cheerful cartoon guests waits behind a velvet rope. Funny, warm, bright.

slides.text: Without the app, your AI explains the job. With it, your AI does the job.
slides.save: 💾 Save this for the next "what's an MCP app?"
